question.problem:
Suppose we wish to find a critical point of the function $f(x,y)$ in the region $[0,1]\times [0,1]⊆{R}^{2},$ where $$ f(x,y)=6x{y}^{2}-3{x}^{2}-6xy+2x. $$ Fill in the blanks in the matrix equation below that defines the first iteration of the Newton-Raphson process starting at the point $[0,\,1]^{T},$ and compute the components of the first iteration. Round the answer for ${x}_{1}$ to **three decimal places**.
$[$ {{field-1}} $6$ $]({x}_{1}-{x}_{0})\,=[$ $-2$ $]$
$6$ {{field-2}} {{field-3}}
${x}_{1}≈[$ $0$ $]$
{{field-4}}
question.worked_solution:
The Newton-Raphson method of optimizing a multivariable function $f:{R}^{n}\to R$ is

$$
{x}_{n+1}={x}_{n}-[{H}_{f}({x}_{n})]^{-1}∇f({x}_{n}),
$$

where $H({x}_{n})$ and $∇f({x}_{n})$ are the Hessian and gradient of $f$, respectively, evaluated at ${x}_{n}.$

Equivalently, at each iteration, the above equation can be rewritten as

$$
{H}_{f}({x}_{n})({x}_{n+1}-{x}_{n})=-∇f({x}_{n}).
$$

In our case, the gradient is

$$
\begin{aligned}∇f(x) & =[\begin{aligned}\frac{∂}{∂x}(6x{y}^{2}-3{x}^{2}-6xy+2x) \\ \frac{∂}{∂y}(6x{y}^{2}-3{x}^{2}-6xy+2x)\end{aligned}] \\  & =[\begin{aligned}6{y}^{2}-6x-6y+2 \\ 12xy-6x\end{aligned}],\end{aligned}
$$

and the Hessian is

$$
\begin{aligned}{H}_{f}(x) & =[\begin{aligned}\frac{∂}{∂x}(6{y}^{2}-6x-6y+2) & \frac{∂}{∂x}(12xy-6x) \\ \frac{∂}{∂y}(6{y}^{2}-6x-6y+2) & \frac{∂}{∂y}(12xy-6x)\end{aligned}] \\  & =[\begin{aligned}-6 & 12y-6 \\ 12y-6 & 12x\end{aligned}].\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, our Newton-Raphson system of equations is

$$
{[\begin{aligned}-6 & 12y-6 \\ 12y-6 & 12x\end{aligned}]}_{{x}_{n}}({x}_{n+1}-{x}_{n})=-{[\begin{aligned}6{y}^{2}-6x-6y+2 \\ 12xy-6x\end{aligned}]}_{{x}_{n}}.
$$

Starting with ${x}_{0}=[\begin{aligned}0 \\ 1\end{aligned}],$ we have

$$
\begin{aligned}{[\begin{aligned}-6 & 12y-6 \\ 12y-6 & 12x\end{aligned}]}_{{x}_{0}}({x}_{1}-{x}_{0}) & =-{[\begin{aligned}6{y}^{2}-6x-6y+2 \\ 12xy-6x\end{aligned}]}_{{x}_{0}} \\ [\begin{aligned}-6 & 12(1)-6 \\ 12(1)-6 & 12(0)\end{aligned}]({x}_{1}-{x}_{0}) & =-[\begin{aligned}6(1)^{2}-6(0)-6(1)+2 \\ 12(0)(1)-6(0)\end{aligned}] \\ [\begin{aligned}-6 & 6 \\ 6 & 0\end{aligned}]({x}_{1}-{x}_{0}) & =[\begin{aligned}-2 \\ 0\end{aligned}].\end{aligned}
$$

Solving this system of equations, we get $({x}_{1}-{x}_{0})=[\begin{aligned}0 \\ -1/3\end{aligned}].$ Hence,

$$
\begin{aligned}{x}_{1} & ={x}_{0}+[\begin{aligned}0 \\ -\frac{1}{3}\end{aligned}] \\  & =[\begin{aligned}0 \\ 1\end{aligned}]+[\begin{aligned}0 \\ -\frac{1}{3}\end{aligned}] \\  & ≈[\begin{aligned}0 \\ 0.667\end{aligned}].\end{aligned}
$$
